text: Nearly a thousand PhDs got this puzzle wrong. Your turn.
Three briefcases, one has a million bucks. You pick one.
The host knows where the money is, and always opens an empty one.
Then he offers a swap. Fifty-fifty, right?
Hit like if you said fifty-fifty.
Nope. Your first pick was a one in three guess. Opening a case didn't change that.
So switching wins two out of three.
Send this to the friend who's— who's already typing 'no way'.
A columnist printed that in nineteen ninety. By her count, nearly a thousand PhDs wrote in to say she's wrong.
Don't buy it? Follow, this page ends the argument.
Make it a hundred cases. You pick one, and he opens ninety-eight empties.
Now switching wins ninety-nine percent. Same game.
So… stay or switch? Your turn.
